# 1. Load & Prepare Data

```{r load-data}
load_cs <- function(path) {
  df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df$month <- as.Date(df$month)
  
  # Contiguous integer period index (1..T): dense rank of months. Replaces the
  # old YYYY*100+MM coding, which distorts dynamic event time at year boundaries
  # (Dec -> Jan jumps by 89). Built identically to the techtagged sibling.
  mfloor      <- as.Date(format(df$month, "%Y-%m-01"))
  u_periods   <- sort(unique(mfloor))
  period_idx  <- setNames(seq_along(u_periods), as.character(u_periods))
  df$period   <- as.integer(period_idx[as.character(mfloor)])

  # g_period on the same contiguous scale (0 = never-treated). Kept NUMERIC
  # (double), not integer: did recodes never-treated groups to Inf internally,
  # which an integer column cannot hold (-> NA -> rows dropped -> "No valid groups").
  df$g <- as.character(df$g)
  df$g[df$g == "" | df$g == "NA"] <- NA
  g_floor     <- as.Date(format(as.Date(df$g), "%Y-%m-01"))
  df$g_period <- period_idx[as.character(g_floor)]
  df$g_period[is.na(df$g_period)] <- 0L
  df$g_period <- as.numeric(df$g_period)
  
  # Firm ID as integer
  df$firm_id <- as.integer(factor(df$Linkedin_name))
  
  # Log outcome
  df$log_collabs <- log1p(df$n_collabs)
  
  df
}

battery_s1  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S1)
battery_s2  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S2)
```

# 2. Callaway & Sant'Anna Estimation

```{r cs-function}
# Primary C&S control group: NEVER-TREATED for BOTH technologies (mirrors the
# techtagged sibling). Some firms are treated in multiple IPCEI rounds, so a
# not-yet-treated firm may already be affected by an earlier treatment and
# contaminate the control pool; never-treated controls avoid this and make the
# two technologies symmetric. (Battery is a single cohort, which independently
# requires never-treated.) The not-yet-treated alternative is one robustness row
# for hydrogen.
cg_for <- function(technology) "nevertreated"

# control_group default was "notyettreated", which contradicted cg_for() and the
# default in _cs_helpers.R. Every call site passes it explicitly, so this default
# never fired and aligning it changes no estimate; it removes the trap of a
# future call silently using the wrong comparison group. Same fix as in 07.
run_cs <- function(df, yname = "log_collabs", label = "", xformla = NULL, control_group = "nevertreated", clustervars = NULL) {
  
  cat("\n=== C&S:", label, "===\n")
  
  # Deterministic per-outcome seed: makes every estimate reproducible and
  # independent of how many other outcomes ran earlier in the same session.
  # With a single set.seed() up front, adding one outcome shifts the bootstrap
  # stream for every later run and moves all downstream p-values.
  set.seed(42L + sum(utf8ToInt(paste0(yname, control_group))))
  cs_out <- att_gt(
    yname         = yname,
    tname         = "period",
    idname        = "firm_id",
    gname         = "g_period",
    control_group = control_group,
    clustervars   = clustervars,
    anticipation  = 0,
    bstrap        = TRUE,
    biters        = BITERS,
    panel         = TRUE,
    xformla       = xformla,
    pl            = TRUE,
    data          = df
  )
  
  print(summary(cs_out))
  cs_out
}
```

```{r cs-battery}
# Battery: single cohort → one ATT(g,t) per post-treatment period

cs_battery_s1 <- run_cs(battery_s1, label = "Battery Spec 1 (balance)", control_group = cg_for("battery"), clustervars = "firm_id")
cs_battery_s2 <- run_cs(battery_s2, label = "Battery Spec 2 (power)", control_group = cg_for("battery"), clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-hydrogen}
# Hydrogen

cs_hydrogen_s1 <- run_cs(hydrogen_s1, label = "Hydrogen Spec 1 (balance)", control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"), clustervars = "firm_id")
cs_hydrogen_s2 <- run_cs(hydrogen_s2, label = "Hydrogen Spec 2 (power)", control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"), clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-robustness}
# Robustness: not-yet-treated controls as one shown alternative to the primary
# never-treated choice. Hydrogen only -- battery is a single cohort with no
# not-yet-treated units (att_gt would fail "No valid groups"). Firm clustering
# is kept to match the primary spec.
cs_hydrogen_notyet <- run_cs(hydrogen_s1,
                             label = "Hydrogen (primary, not-yet-treated)",
                             control_group = "notyettreated",
                             clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-aggregate}

agg_simple  <- function(cs_out) aggte(cs_out, type = "simple")
agg_dynamic <- function(cs_out) aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic",
                                      min_e = -12, max_e = 24)

pval_from_att <- function(att, se) {
  round(2 * pnorm(-abs(att / se)), 3)
}

# Pre-trend test. Primary is did's universal Wald pre-test (cs_out$Wpval). For
# staggered designs that bootstrap covariance is singular and att_gt returns no
# Wald (hydrogen, confirmed -- it stays NULL under never- AND not-yet-treated).
# In that case fall back to a joint test that the pre-period (e < 0) dynamic
# event-study coefficients are zero: a chi-square of their t-statistics from
# aggte(type="dynamic") att.egt/se.egt (analytic SEs, df = # pre-periods). The
# `method` field records which test was used.
es_pretrend <- function(cs_out) {
  if (is.null(cs_out)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  if (!is.null(cs_out$Wpval))
    return(list(stat = round(cs_out$W, 3), p = round(cs_out$Wpval, 3), method = "Wald"))
  dyn <- tryCatch(
    aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24, bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(dyn)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  pre <- dyn$egt < 0
  t2  <- (dyn$att.egt[pre] / dyn$se.egt[pre])^2
  ok  <- is.finite(t2); k <- sum(ok)
  if (k == 0) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  stat <- sum(t2[ok])
  list(stat = round(stat, 3), p = round(1 - pchisq(stat, df = k), 3), method = "ES-joint")
}

sample_stats <- function(df, yname) {
  df_use <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[yname]]),
      !is.na(firm_id),
      !is.na(period),
      !is.na(g_period)
    )

  data.frame(
    N_obs     = nrow(df_use),
    N_units   = n_distinct(df_use$firm_id),
    N_treated = n_distinct(df_use$firm_id[df_use$g_period > 0]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

make_att_row <- function(agg_obj, label, type, cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) {
    sample_stats(df, yname)
  } else {
    data.frame(N_obs = NA_integer_, N_units = NA_integer_, N_treated = NA_integer_)
  }

  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Specification    = label,
    Type             = type,
    ATT              = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE               = round(agg_obj$overall.se,  4),
    p_value          = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs            = stats$N_obs,
    N_units          = stats$N_units,
    N_treated        = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

make_att_row_std <- function(agg_obj, technology, outcome, type,
                             cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) {
    sample_stats(df, yname)
  } else {
    data.frame(N_obs = NA_integer_, N_units = NA_integer_, N_treated = NA_integer_)
  }

  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Technology       = technology,
    Outcome          = outcome,
    Type             = type,
    ATT              = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE               = round(agg_obj$overall.se,  4),
    p_value          = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs            = stats$N_obs,
    N_units          = stats$N_units,
    N_treated        = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# ── Primary specs: simple ATT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
agg_battery_s1_simple  <- agg_simple(cs_battery_s1)
agg_battery_s2_simple  <- agg_simple(cs_battery_s2)
agg_hydrogen_s1_simple <- agg_simple(cs_hydrogen_s1)
agg_hydrogen_s2_simple <- agg_simple(cs_hydrogen_s2)

# ── Primary specs: dynamic (event study) ─────────────────────────────────────
agg_battery_s1_dyn  <- agg_dynamic(cs_battery_s1)
agg_battery_s2_dyn  <- agg_dynamic(cs_battery_s2)
agg_hydrogen_s1_dyn <- agg_dynamic(cs_hydrogen_s1)
agg_hydrogen_s2_dyn <- agg_dynamic(cs_hydrogen_s2)

# ── Robustness check: simple ATT (not-yet-treated controls, hydrogen only) ────
agg_hydrogen_notyet_simple <- agg_simple(cs_hydrogen_notyet)

# ── ATT summary table (Specification schema — for main Rmd display) ──────────
att_table <- bind_rows(
  make_att_row(agg_hydrogen_s1_simple, "Hydrogen", "Primary",
               cs_out = cs_hydrogen_s1, df = hydrogen_s1, yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row(agg_battery_s1_simple,  "Battery",  "Primary",
               cs_out = cs_battery_s1,  df = battery_s1,  yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row(agg_hydrogen_s2_simple, "Hydrogen", "Larger control group",
               cs_out = cs_hydrogen_s2, df = hydrogen_s2, yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row(agg_battery_s2_simple,  "Battery",  "Larger control group",
               cs_out = cs_battery_s2,  df = battery_s2,  yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row(agg_hydrogen_notyet_simple, "Hydrogen", "Not-yet-treated controls",
               cs_out = cs_hydrogen_notyet, df = hydrogen_s1, yname = "log_collabs")
)

cat("\n=== Overall ATT Summary ===\n")
print(att_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(att_table, "../results/psm/intensity/att_summary_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 3. Power simulation (total collaborations)

Simulate on real control-group data to preserve the empirical variance and
autocorrelation structure, then inject an artificial ATT and record the
rejection rate at the 5% level
(Egerod & Hollenbach 2024; Black et al. 2022).

Total collaboration is insignificant in both technologies ($p = 0.253$ battery,
$p = 0.275$ hydrogen), so power evidence would decide whether "no detectable
change in total collaboration" means no change or means the design cannot see
one. It is reported alongside the composition outcomes, whose power curves are
produced by `07_..._psm.Rmd` on the same effect grid.

**Open decision (Nov 2026): whether this outcome belongs in the SI power
figure at all.** Total collaboration is the sum of the technology-related and
technology-unrelated rows of Table 1, where the first is positive and the second
is a precise zero, so its null is arithmetic rather than a finding: an increase
concentrated in one component, diluted by a larger component that does not move.
No claim in the paper rests on it. It is also the weakest-powered cell in the
whole design (battery spec 1 reaches only 0.53 power against a 20% effect), so
including it invites "the design is underpowered" as a blanket charge instead of
a statement about one aggregate. Leave `RUN_POWER <- FALSE` here unless the
manuscript asserts somewhere that overall collaboration volume did not rise, in
which case that claim needs this curve and the honest number has to be reported.

**RESOLVED (18 Nov 2026): the condition is met, so this outcome IS simulated.**
`RUN_POWER` stays `FALSE` in the setup chunk purely so a plain knit remains
fast; the power chunks are run deliberately, with the flag overridden, exactly
as section 9 of script 07 is. The
results section states "Total collaboration rises by 21% for battery firms
($p = 0.253$) and 10% for hydrogen firms ($p = 0.275$), neither of which is
statistically significant", and that sentence carries part of the
redirection-rather-than-general-rise argument. Two warnings attach to the
number this produces. First, the 0.53 quoted above came from the
placebo-from-controls design, which overstated power everywhere, so the
corrected battery figure will be LOWER, not higher. Second, battery's size
check runs hot (0.067--0.084 on the composition cells at 29 clusters), so read
the zero row before quoting the MDE. If the honest curve turns out too weak to
support the sentence, the fix is to delete the sentence, not to hide the curve:
the technology-unrelated benchmark already carries the redirection argument and
is the better evidence for it.

The simulation function itself now lives in `_cs_helpers.R`, so this file and
07 run the same code. Two things changed when it moved: the control group is
passed in rather than defaulting to not-yet-treated, and every cell is seeded
from its own (outcome, label, effect size), so a run is reproducible whatever
else ran before it in the session.

Output is `power_intensity_long.csv`, in the same long schema as
`power_all_outcomes.csv` so notebook 08 can stack them into one SI figure. The
older wide `power_simulation_results.csv` is left on disk and superseded.

```{r power-helpers}
.power_env <- new.env()
sys.source("_cs_helpers.R", envir = .power_env)
run_power_sim  <- .power_env$run_power_sim
mde_at         <- .power_env$mde_at
POWER_PCT_GRID <- .power_env$POWER_PCT_GRID   # 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 (%)
POWER_LOG_GRID <- .power_env$POWER_LOG_GRID   # the same grid in log points

# Draws per (cell, effect size). The Monte Carlo SE of a power estimate is at
# most 0.5/sqrt(n_sims), so 2.2 points at 500.
N_SIMS_POWER <- 500   # matched to section 9 of script 07; see the note there

# Zero is prepended to the grid as a size check, and 199 bootstrap draws run
# inside each simulated draw. Both mirror section 9 of script 07; the reasoning
# is in the run_power_sim header in _cs_helpers.R.
POWER_GRID_RUN <- c(0, POWER_LOG_GRID)
BITERS_SIM     <- 199

# The effect sizes of a cell run in parallel, so one core per size keeps a
# cell to a single draw-batch of wall clock. Leave one core for the machine.
POWER_CORES <- max(1L, min(length(POWER_GRID_RUN),
                           parallel::detectCores() - 1L))

# Total collaborations across all technologies: the reported intensity outcome.
POWER_OUTCOME <- "log_collabs"

# Spec 2 (larger control group) doubles the runtime and is a robustness check,
# not a reported estimate. Off by default.
RUN_POWER_SPEC2 <- FALSE
```

```{r power-cells}
power_cells <- list(
  list(Technology = "Battery",  Spec = "Spec 1", df = battery_s1),
  list(Technology = "Hydrogen", Spec = "Spec 1", df = hydrogen_s1)
)
if (RUN_POWER_SPEC2) power_cells <- c(power_cells, list(
  list(Technology = "Battery",  Spec = "Spec 2", df = battery_s2),
  list(Technology = "Hydrogen", Spec = "Spec 2", df = hydrogen_s2)
))

cat("\n=== Power cells ===\n")
for (cell in power_cells)
  cat(sprintf("  %-9s %-7s  N firms = %d\n", cell$Technology, cell$Spec,
              length(unique(cell$df$Linkedin_name))))
stopifnot(POWER_OUTCOME %in% names(battery_s1),
          POWER_OUTCOME %in% names(hydrogen_s1))
```

```{r power-timing, eval=RUN_POWER}
# Budget the run before starting it: time one draw per cell and extrapolate.
for (cell in power_cells) {
  el <- system.time(
    run_power_sim(cell$df, POWER_OUTCOME, POWER_LOG_GRID[1],
                  cg_for(tolower(cell$Technology)), n_sims = 2,
                  label = paste("timing", cell$Technology, cell$Spec),
                  biters_sim = BITERS_SIM)
  )[["elapsed"]] / 2
  tot <- el * N_SIMS_POWER * length(POWER_GRID_RUN)
  cat(sprintf("%-9s %-7s %.2f s/draw -> %.2f h serial for this cell\n",
              cell$Technology, cell$Spec, el, tot / 3600))
}
cat("Divide by mc.cores for the wall-clock estimate.\n")
```

```{r power-run, eval=RUN_POWER}
library(parallel)

# Robust parallelism: fork when available, fall back to serial if the fork
# workers fail (e.g. a non-interactive session), so an overnight run never
# silently returns no results.
mclapply <- function(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = min(4L, parallel::detectCores())) {
  res <- tryCatch(parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = mc.cores),
                  error = function(e) base::lapply(X, FUN))
  if (any(vapply(res, function(z) inherits(z, "try-error"), logical(1))))
    res <- base::lapply(X, FUN)
  res
}

power_rows <- list()
for (cell in power_cells) {
  lbl <- paste(cell$Technology, "--", cell$Spec, "-- Total collaborations")
  cat("Power simulation:", lbl, "\n")

  # The reported estimate for this technology, so the CSV carries the same
  # ATT / p_value columns as the composition file, and so att_hat can impose
  # the null: the estimated effect is removed from the treated firms'
  # post-periods before the hypothesised one is added, making the true effect
  # in a draw `a` rather than `a` on top of what the data already contain.
  ref <- att_table[att_table$Specification == cell$Technology &
                     att_table$Type == "Primary", , drop = FALSE]
  att_ref <- if (nrow(ref)) ref$ATT[1] else 0

  grid_rows <- mclapply(POWER_GRID_RUN, function(a)
    run_power_sim(cell$df, POWER_OUTCOME, a,
                  cg_for(tolower(cell$Technology)),
                  n_sims = N_SIMS_POWER, label = lbl,
                  att_hat = att_ref, biters_sim = BITERS_SIM),
    mc.cores = POWER_CORES)
  grid_rows <- grid_rows[!vapply(grid_rows, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (!length(grid_rows)) next

  out <- do.call(rbind, grid_rows)
  out$Technology  <- cell$Technology
  out$Outcome     <- "Total collaborations"
  out$Type        <- "Benchmark"
  out$key         <- "intensity"
  out$yname       <- POWER_OUTCOME
  out$Spec        <- cell$Spec
  out$ATT         <- if (nrow(ref)) ref$ATT[1] else NA_real_
  out$p_value     <- if (nrow(ref)) ref$p_value[1] else NA_real_
  out$significant <- !is.na(out$p_value) & out$p_value < 0.10
  power_rows[[length(power_rows) + 1]] <- out
}

power_intensity <- do.call(rbind, power_rows)
power_intensity <- power_intensity[, c("Technology", "Outcome", "Type", "key",
                                       "yname", "Spec", "att_log", "att_pct",
                                       "power", "n_draws", "n_sims", "ATT",
                                       "p_value", "significant")]
print(power_intensity, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(power_intensity,
          "../results/psm/intensity/power_intensity_long.csv", row.names = FALSE)

bad <- power_intensity[power_intensity$n_draws < power_intensity$n_sims, ]
if (nrow(bad)) {
  cat("\n!! draws that did not converge:\n"); print(bad, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r power-mde, eval=RUN_POWER}
power_mde_int <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(power_intensity, list(power_intensity$Technology, power_intensity$Spec),
        drop = TRUE),
  function(d) data.frame(
    Technology  = d$Technology[1],
    Spec        = d$Spec[1],
    Outcome     = "Total collaborations",
    ATT         = d$ATT[1],
    p_value     = d$p_value[1],
    mde_pct     = round(mde_at(d$att_pct, d$power, 0.80), 1),
    power_at_10 = d$power[which.min(abs(d$att_pct - 10))],
    power_at_20 = d$power[which.min(abs(d$att_pct - 20))],
    # Rejection rate at a true effect of zero; must sit near 0.05 or the MDE
    # on that row is void. Read this before quoting anything.
    size        = d$power[which(abs(d$att_log) < 1e-12)[1]],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
cat("\n=== Minimum detectable effect at 80% power ===\n")
cat("NA = the curve never reaches 80% over the grid tested.\n")
print(power_mde_int, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(power_mde_int, "../results/psm/intensity/power_mde_intensity.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 5. Export long-format results (per-folder, for notebook 08)

Writes long-format CSVs into this file's own `results/intensity/` folder, mirroring
the `07_ck_didestimation_composition_techtagged` export schema, so notebook 08 can
read the overall-total ("intensity") reference outcome from a clean per-folder
source instead of the legacy `results/event_study_all.csv` / `results/att_summary_all.csv`.
The legacy writes above are intentionally KEPT until 08 is repointed and verified.

```{r export-intensity}
INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT <- "month"   # this file is monthly (YYYYMM coding); no quarterly toggle

# 1) Dynamic event study (long): one row per (Technology, Outcome, e).
#    SAME 95% CI convention (att +/- 1.96*se) and SAME "<Technology> -- <Outcome>"
#    label convention as the composition export, so 08 reads both identically.
export_dynamic <- function(agg_dyn, technology, outcome) {
  .crit <- if (!is.null(agg_dyn$crit.val.egt) && is.finite(agg_dyn$crit.val.egt))
    agg_dyn$crit.val.egt else qnorm(0.975)   # simultaneous band when available
  data.frame(
    label      = sprintf("%s -- %s", technology, outcome),
    Technology = technology,
    Outcome    = outcome,
    e          = agg_dyn$egt,
    att        = agg_dyn$att.egt,
    se         = agg_dyn$se.egt,
    ci_lower   = agg_dyn$att.egt - .crit * agg_dyn$se.egt,
    ci_upper   = agg_dyn$att.egt + .crit * agg_dyn$se.egt,
    TimeUnit   = INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# This file estimates a single outcome (total/intensity); export the primary-spec
# (S2) dynamic ATTs for battery and hydrogen.
event_study_intensity <- bind_rows(
  export_dynamic(agg_battery_s1_dyn,  "Battery",  "Total collabs"),
  export_dynamic(agg_hydrogen_s1_dyn, "Hydrogen", "Total collabs")
)

write.csv(event_study_intensity,
          "../results/psm/intensity/event_study_intensity.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 2) Overall ATT summary in the SAME schema as att_techtagged_table.csv:
#    Technology, Outcome, Type, TimeUnit, ATT, SE, p_value, pretrend_*, N_*.
att_summary_intensity <- bind_rows(
  make_att_row_std(agg_battery_s1_simple,  "Battery",  "Total collabs", "Primary",
                   cs_out = cs_battery_s1,  df = battery_s1,  yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row_std(agg_hydrogen_s1_simple, "Hydrogen", "Total collabs", "Primary",
                   cs_out = cs_hydrogen_s1, df = hydrogen_s1, yname = "log_collabs")
)
att_summary_intensity$TimeUnit <- INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT
att_summary_intensity <- att_summary_intensity[, c(
  "Technology", "Outcome", "Type", "TimeUnit", "ATT", "SE", "p_value",
  "pretrend_stat", "pretrend_p_value", "pretrend_test", "N_obs", "N_units", "N_treated"
)]

write.csv(att_summary_intensity,
          "../results/psm/intensity/att_summary_intensity.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n--- Per-folder intensity exports ---\n")
cat("event_study_intensity.csv:", nrow(event_study_intensity), "rows; labels:",
    paste(unique(event_study_intensity$label), collapse = " | "), "\n")
cat("att_summary_intensity.csv:", nrow(att_summary_intensity), "rows\n")
```

# Notes for paper

- **Outcome variable**: log_collabs — log-transformed monthly collaboration count. 
- **Estimator**: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021, *Journal of Econometrics*),
  primary control group = never-treated (both technologies), firm-level clustered
  SEs, bootstrap inference (999 iterations); not-yet-treated shown as robustness.
- **Power simulation**: 150 runs per ATT level, DGP drawn from real control-group 
  data to preserve empirical variance and autocorrelation structure 
  (Egerod & Hollenbach 2024; Black et al. 2022).
- **Sensitivity**: Rosenbaum bounds (Rosenbaum 2002) using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. 
  Gamma threshold reported as the level of unmeasured confounding that would 
  render the pre-treatment balance test insignificant.
- **MDE interpretation**: Report minimum detectable effect in percent terms 
  (exp(MDE_log) - 1), which is directly interpretable as a % change in 
  monthly collaborations.
